Resolves #19886

Both header buttons now announce their sort direction through `aria-sort`, written next to the class mutation that
already produced the arrow: `ascending` for `'ASC'`, `descending` for `'DESC'`, and removed when the header is
unsorted. The attribute is set in `afterSetIsSorted()` and cleared in `removeSortingCss()`, because that method
resets `_isSorted` directly and never reaches the setter — a header cleared from the header menu would otherwise
keep announcing a direction it no longer has. Keeping the write in the same place as the class means the glyph and
the announced direction cannot drift apart.

Evidence: L3 (headless Chromium against a live `npm run server-start` on `localhost:8080`, attributes read with
`getAttribute` off the rendered DOM) → L3 required (AC-1 and AC-2 name an attribute on a rendered element, which
`vdom` state alone does not prove is in the document). Residual: none.

Outside CI: DOM read against the live server, under `## Test Evidence`. |

| AC-3 | CI-covered: `npm run test-unit -- test/playwright/unit/grid/HeaderButtonSortable.spec.mjs` — the file covers `sortable: false` plus the three states for both buttons. The suite was green at 4 passed; the two new cases also fail against unmodified `dev`, which is what makes them non-vacuous, under `## Test Evidence`. |

## Deltas from ticket

**The two files write to different nodes, on purpose.** The ticket says to set `aria-sort` "in both header buttons",
and for the grid that is exactly what happens: the button carrying `role: 'columnheader'` *is* the node
`getVdomRoot()` returns, so the write goes through `changeVdomRootKey('aria-sort', …)` beside the existing `role`
and `height` writes.

The table is not the same shape. Its columnheader is the `<th>` the button sits in — the button keeps `role=button`,
and `getVdomRoot()` points at it deliberately, since top-level style attributes belong on the inner element. Writing
`aria-sort` there would put it on a `role=button`, where WAI-ARIA 1.2 does not allow it and no screen reader
announces it, so the table half writes `me.vdom` instead. Verified in the DOM: the element that receives the
attribute is a native `<th>` (`role=null`, i.e. the implicit columnheader), not the button.

**One extra `update()` on the table side.** A grid header that is already `neo-sort-hidden` still gets an update from
`changeVdomRootKey()`. On the table side `removeSortingCss()` writes the same `cls` array back on every branch, which
produces no update when nothing else changed, so the stale attribute would survive. The explicit `update()` covers
the case the grid gets for free.

**State lives in two places now, and the class cannot be used to infer it.** `case null:` only adds
`neo-sort-hidden` and leaves `neo-sort-desc` on the header, so after a header is cleared it still matches
`neo-sort-desc` while carrying no `aria-sort`. Reading the CSS class as a proxy for the sort state was already
wrong for a second reason — `sortable: false` sets the same hidden class — so the attribute is tracked on its own
rather than derived from `cls`.

## Test Evidence

All coverage runs in CI. The receipts a green suite cannot show are the two DOM reads, run against
`npm run server-start` with `getAttribute` before and after a click:

`[QUARANTINED_URL: localhost:8080]` — initial state, where the `#` column starts sorted:

```
#        role=columnheader  aria-sort=descending   arrow=true
Title    role=columnheader  aria-sort=null         arrow=false
```

after clicking `Title`:

```
#        aria-sort=null        arrow=true
Title    aria-sort=ascending   arrow=true
```

`[QUARANTINED_URL: localhost:8080]` — nothing carries the attribute initially; after
clicking `Firstname`:

```
TH Firstname  aria-sort=ascending
TH Lastname   aria-sort=null
```

Exactly one header carries the attribute at a time and it moves with the sort, which is the shape WAI-ARIA asks
for.

Reverse check on the new cases: with `src/grid/header/Button.mjs` and `src/table/header/Button.mjs` restored to
`dev`, both report `Received: undefined`. So they fail for the reason the ticket describes rather than passing
whatever the source does.

## Post-Merge Validation

- [ ] Announcement on real assistive technology: the DOM carries `aria-sort` per the reads above, but whether NVDA

      a real screen reader, which this sandbox cannot drive.

### `@sunred-liu` commented on 2026-10-20T11:36:52Z

Checked the unit cases against a real DOM as well, since the unit tier only sees `vdom` and the risk in a
change like this is that the write never reaches the element. Ran `npm run server-start` and inspected the two
examples from the issue with DevTools' own `getAttribute`, before and after a click.

`[QUARANTINED_URL: localhost:8080]` — initial state, the `#` column starts sorted:

```
BUTTON #        role=columnheader  aria-sort=descending   arrow=true
BUTTON Title    role=columnheader  aria-sort=null         arrow=false
BUTTON Summary  role=columnheader  aria-sort=null         arrow=false
...
```

after clicking `Title`:

```
BUTTON #        aria-sort=null        arrow=true
BUTTON Title    aria-sort=ascending   arrow=true
BUTTON Summary  aria-sort=null        arrow=false
```

`[QUARANTINED_URL: localhost:8080]` — a native `<th>` (`role=null`, i.e. the implicit
columnheader), which is what the table half writes to. Initially nothing carries the attribute; after clicking
`Firstname`:

```
TH Firstname  aria-sort=ascending
TH Lastname   aria-sort=null
TH Github Id  aria-sort=null
```

Both are the shape WAI-ARIA asks for: exactly one header carries `aria-sort` at a time, and it moves with the sort.

One thing that fell out of the same check, and is worth knowing for anyone reading the class instead: `case null:`
only adds `neo-sort-hidden` and leaves `neo-sort-desc` on the header, so after the click above `#` still matches
`neo-sort-desc` while carrying no `aria-sort`. The class is not a usable proxy for the state — the attribute has to
be tracked on its own, which is what this PR does.
